newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cargo ship heads back to Singapore after hijack.
newsitem.headline: Cargo ship heads back to Singapore after hijack.

text.p: A cargo ship and crew hijacked for six days by pirates off Malaysia headed back to Singapore on Tuesday after being freed, newspapers reported on Tuesday.
The pirates had hijacked the Belize-registered MV Wint Thai in the South China Sea, held the crew and stole its load of cigarettes, the newspapers said.
The ship went missing on March 4 after leaving Singapore for South Korea, maritime newspaper Lloyd's List and Singapore's Straits Times newspaper said.
The Straits Times said the pirates stole cigarettes worth Singapore $5 million (US$3.5 million) during a six-day hijacking in which they handcuffed the mainly Burmese and Indonesian crew.

"There were about 10 of them. They came in a big speed boat, fired three shots into the air and jumped on board. Then they handcuffed us, kicked us and beat us with their rifles. Some of us are bleeding," the Straits Times quoted Wint Thai captain Mauang Soe Paing as saying.
It said the pirates took all the ship's documents, charts, books, crew passports and radio equipment.

But they missed one radio, which the crew used to alert officials at the International Maritime Bureau Piracy Centre in Kuala Lumpur to the hijacking on Monday after the pirates released them, Lloyd's List said.
According to Lloyd's, the captain told the piracy centre the vessel was hijacked in the early hours of March 5 off peninsula Malaysia's east coast.
The Straits Times said the vessel's owner had mounted an unsuccessful aerial search when he could not contact the crew. It said the pirates had renamed the ship to evade detection.
The reports said the Wint Thai was making its way back to Singapore.
Officials at the Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore and the Singapore Police Coastguard said they could not confirm the report.
